rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Theories of evolution progressed from Lamarck's inheritance of acquired traits (rejected) to Darwin's natural selection (variation, struggle, survival of the fittest) to Neo-Darwinism (modern synthesis), which integrates Mendelian genetics with selection, genetic drift, gene flow, and recombination.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Hardy-Weinberg: p² + 2pq + q² = 1 (p = dominant allele freq, q = recessive)
Natural selection: variation → struggle → survival of fittest → adaptation
Evolution (modern): change in allele frequencies in a population over generations

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Lamarck's "inheritance of acquired characteristics" is largely rejected: a muscle built by exercise is NOT passed to offspring.  ·  Darwin did NOT know about genes; his mechanism (natural selection) was later explained by genetics (Neo-Darwinism).

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: NEB expects a clear Lamarck vs Darwin comparison.  ·  The modern synthesis (Neo-Darwinism) is the "correct" current theory; know its components.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Lamarck: giraffes stretched necks → passed longer necks (rejected).  ·  Darwin: peppered moth (Biston betularia) — industrial melanism (dark form favoured post-industrial).

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Natural selection acts on VARIATION in a population; it does not create new traits (mutations create variation).  ·  Genetic drift is a random change in allele frequency (important in small populations); natural selection is NON-random (directed by fitness).

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Compare Lamarck vs Darwin  ·  Explain modern synthesis

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Lamarck = L-A-M (Learned, Acquired, Modified) traits — inherited (wrong).  ·  Darwin = D-N-S (Difference, Nature, Selection) — survival of the fittest.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: Explain Lamarck's theory and why it is largely rejected.  ·  Describe the postulates of Darwin's theory of natural selection.

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: Compare Lamarckism and Darwinism (postulates, example, status).  ·  Describe the modern synthesis (Neo-Darwinism).

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Lamarckism  ·  Darwinism (natural selection)  ·  Neo-Darwinism (modern synthesis)  ·  Genetic drift

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Lamarckism: use/disuse + inheritance of acquired traits (rejected).  ·  Darwinism: natural selection; variation, overproduction, survival of fittest.  ·  Neo-Darwinism: genetics + selection + drift + gene flow + recombination.  ·  Evolution = change in allele frequencies in a population.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Darwin's 1859 book "On the Origin of Species" laid out natural selection.  ·  Lamarck published "Philosophie Zoologique" (1809), proposing inheritance of acquired traits.

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: What is Neo-Darwinism (the modern synthesis)?  ·  Differentiate natural selection from genetic drift.  ·  State the Hardy-Weinberg principle and the conditions for equilibrium.

rows.label: More hints
rows.text: State the Hardy-Weinberg principle and conditions.  ·  Give a real-world example of observed natural selection (antibiotic resistance).

rows.label: Extra solved
rows.text: Antibiotic resistance: a few resistant bacteria survive → become the population (selection).  ·  Genetic drift: founder effect in island populations (random allele change).

rows.label: MCQ drill
rows.text: Lamarck's idea of "inheritance of acquired characteristics" is now: → B  ·  The "modern synthesis" (Neo-Darwinism) integrates natural selection with: → B

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: Lamarckism (Lamarck, 1809): "use and disuse" of organs + "inheritance of acquired characteristics"; organisms change during life and pass on acquired traits. Mostly rejected (no mechanism for heredity).  ·  Darwinism (Darwin, 1859): natural selection; variation exists in populations; overproduction leads to struggle for existence; organisms better adapted survive and reproduce (survival of the fittest).  ·  Neo-Darwinism (synthetic theory, early 20th c.): integrates Mendelian genetics with natural selection; evolution = change in allele frequencies in a population; mechanisms: mutation, recombination, natural selection, genetic drift, gene flow.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Gene flow  ·  Hardy-Weinberg  ·  Antibiotic resistance

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Use vs disuse  ·  evolvere = unrolling/unfolding) is a gradual and orderly change from one state to another.  ·  Charles Darwin defined it as "descent with modification".

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: It's important to note that evolution isn't about changes happening to one individual during its lifetime; rather, it's about how entire groups of organisms change over many generations.  ·  Simple organisms in the past evolved to present-day complex organisms adapting to Earth's changing environment.  ·  Evolution can also be defined as a slow, continuous, and irreversible journey from primitive life forms to today's advanced organisms.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Natural selection is non-random; genetic drift is random.  ·  Hardy-Weinberg: p² + 2pq + q² = 1 (equilibrium when no evolution).  ·  Neo-Darwinism = modern synthesis = genetics + natural selection + drift + gene flow + recombination.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Evolution is NOT goal-oriented; there is no "progress" toward a goal, only adaptation to current environments.  ·  Distinguish between key concepts in Theories of Evolution.  ·  Understand the differences between similar topics.
